pr.title: Transmute from NonNull to pointer when elaborating a box deref (MCP807)
pr.description:
Since per https://github.com/rust-lang/compiler-team/issues/807 we have to stop projecting into `NonNull`.

cc https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/133652
pr.author: scottmcm

processing.reason: The PR is a representation change mandated by MCP#807, not an observable semantic rewrite. Historically ElaborateBoxDerefs produced `copy (((_1.0: Unique<T>).0: NonNull<T>).0: *const T)`; the fix produces `copy ((_1.0: Unique<T>).0: NonNull<T>) as *const T (Transmute)`. In the fixed compiler `NonNull<T>` is a transparent single-pointer wrapper, so reading its `.0` field and transmuting the wrapper to `*const T` yield exactly the same pointer value and provenance for every defined execution. The affected `Box<Never>` cases are followed by `unreachable`/`PlaceMention` and cannot expose a differing observable value, and `box_to_raw_mut` likewise only extracts the same pointer. Ordinary Rust cannot even perform the forbidden private projection into `std::ptr::NonNull`, and modeling it with a custom struct would only reproduce an identical field value. Therefore no source-grounded original/transformed pair with differing defined outputs exists for this PR; constructing one would require an unrelated layout/return-value change.

analysis.summary: ElaborateBoxDerefs must stop expanding a box deref into executable MIR field projections through `NonNull`'s pointer field. The historical rewrite projected `Unique.0 -> NonNull.0 -> *const T`; the corrected pass projects only to `NonNull` and emits `Rvalue::Cast(CastKind::Transmute, ..., ptr_ty)` for executable code, while retaining the extra `NonNull.0 -> ptr` projection only for debug info. The updated GVN, DataflowConstProp, LowerIntrinsics, and SimplifyCfg dumps are consumers of this new MIR shape, not independent pass rewrites.
analysis.originalLogic:
`build_projection` returned three place elements, and the box-deref visitor copied the fully projected pointer field directly:
`[PlaceElem::Field(FieldIdx::ZERO, unique_ty), PlaceElem::Field(FieldIdx::ZERO, nonnull_ty), PlaceElem::Field(FieldIdx::ZERO, ptr_ty)]`.
The executable rewrite was `Rvalue::Use(Operand::Copy(Place::from(place.local).project_deeper(&build_projection(unique_ty, nonnull_ty, ptr_ty), tcx)))`, i.e. it produced MIR such as `copy (((_7.0: Unique<i32>).0: NonNull<i32>).0: *const i32)`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically, ElaborateBoxDerefs projected into `NonNull<_>` in executable basic blocks to reach its inner raw-pointer field. Per the PR, that projection is no longer permitted: “Since per https://github.com/rust-lang/compiler-team/issues/807 we have to stop projecting into `NonNull`.” The wrong transformation is therefore the direct field projection `(...NonNull<T>).0: *const T` in ordinary MIR operations. The fix instead projects only through `Unique.0 -> NonNull<T>` and converts with `Rvalue::Cast(CastKind::Transmute, ..., ptr_ty)`, yielding `copy ((_7.0: Unique<i32>).0: NonNull<i32>) as *const i32 (Transmute)`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR functions whose box dereferences are elaborated after box lowering, including plain box expressions/reads (`tests/mir-opt/box_expr.rs`), `box_to_raw_mut` (`&mut Box<i32>` to `*mut i32`), box-to-raw casts, and transmutes involving uninhabited boxed types (`Box<Never>`). Relevant test variants cover inhabited `i32`, uninhabited `Never`, 32-bit and 64-bit pointer widths, and both panic-abort and panic-unwind.
analysis.trigger: A `Box<T>` dereference is lowered such that ElaborateBoxDerefs replaces the `Box` deref with a pointer-producing projection. The trigger is any executable copy of the box's pointer that the pass elaborates; uninhabited `Box<Never>` transmutes additionally exercise constant propagation of the resulting cast.
preconditions: The pass is elaborating a box deref and has computed `unique_ty`, `nonnull_ty`, and `ptr_ty` via `build_ptr_tys`.
The target MIR follows MCP#807, which forbids projecting into `NonNull<_>` in a basic block.
`build_projection` now has arity 2 and returns only `Unique.0` and `NonNull`; callers needing debug info must append the pointer field themselves.
pitfalls: Do not restore the old three-element `build_projection` or copy `NonNull.0` directly in executable MIR; that is precisely the forbidden projection.

Do not remove the debug-info-only `PlaceElem::Field(FieldIdx::ZERO, ptr_ty)`: the source explicitly says “While we can't project into `NonNull<_>` in a basic block due to MCP#807, this is debug info where it's fine.”
The GVN, DataflowConstProp, LowerIntrinsics, and SimplifyCfg test changes are consequences of consuming the new cast-based MIR, not separate historical bugs in those passes.

Constant-propagation expectations can differ in form: a copy may remain `NonNull<T> as *const T (Transmute)`, while GVN can fold it to `const std::ptr::NonNull::<Never> {{ pointer: {0x1 as *const Never} }} as *const Never (Transmute)`; both must be distinguished from the old direct `...NonNull<Never>).0: *const Never` projection.
analysis.testStrategy: Use mir-opt tests that assert the executable pointer extraction is a transmute cast, e.g. `copy (((_7.0: Unique<i32>).0: NonNull<i32>) as *const i32 (Transmute)`, and assert the absence of `((...NonNull<T>).0: *const T)` in basic-block MIR. Cover `box_expr`, `const_prop/boxes`, `transmute.unreachable_box` under GVN and DataflowConstProp (32-bit and 64-bit), `lower_intrinsics.transmute_to_box_uninhabited`, and `retag.box_to_raw_mut.SimplifyCfg-pre-optimizations` for both panic-abort and panic-unwind. Inspect actual assignments in the decoded diffs rather than relying on retained test labels.
evidence: Since per https://github.com/rust-lang/compiler-team/issues/807 we have to stop projecting into `NonNull`.
// due to MCP#807, this is debug info where it's fine.
// CHECK:   [[ptr:_.*]] = copy (([[box]].0: std::ptr::Unique<S>).0: std::ptr::NonNull<S>) as *const S (Transmute);
+         _2 = const std::ptr::NonNull::<Never> {{ pointer: {0x1 as *const Never} }} as *const Never (Transmute);
